title: Decision: the parent-dependent cascade is a hub proposal, not a hub removal
description:
Needed by bead mimid-1wgh.108. Mark decided 2026-11-23.

THE TEXT. room-policy-04 §5: "If a user leaves or is removed from the
parent room, that user is automatically removed from any
parent-dependent rooms of that parent."

THE PROBLEM. mimid's hub cannot do that. hub/operator.rs states it
plainly: "The hub is not a member and cannot commit". Removing a user
from an MLS group needs a Commit, and only a member makes one. §5 asks
for an action from a party that cannot perform it.

OPTIONS WEIGHED:
(a) Propose the removal, reusing the existing operator-removal path.
(b) Act only by refusing: deny a Commit that would leave the child's
    participants outside the parent's, which the subset check of
    decision mimid-1wgh.110 already does.
(c) Do nothing and raise it upstream as unimplementable by a non-member
    hub.
(d) Propose AND refuse everything in the child until it lands.

CHOSEN: (a), propose it.

WHY:
- The machinery exists and is already trusted for exactly this shape.
  hub/operator.rs feeds a removal "through Hub::update as one proposal
  bundle from its own domain, so they are checked, stored as pending and
  fanned out like any member's proposals", and documents the
  consequence: "the removal takes effect with the next Commit, which
  must include every pending proposal (decision mimid-1wgh.6.5). Until
  then the user is still in the room." The cascade inherits that
  sentence rather than inventing a new caveat.
- It is the closest thing to §5 a non-member hub can do, so mimid
  implements the intent without claiming an ability it lacks.
- (b) is weaker than it looks and was nearly chosen by mistake: the
  subset check fires only when a Commit CARRIES a participant list, so
  the departed user keeps media access and the room keeps working until
  someone changes membership. Worth recording, because it reads like
  enforcement and is not.
- (d) was rejected on a denial-of-service ground: refusing everything in
  the child until the removal commits lets one departed user stall a
  whole call room, and a hostile member of the parent could trigger it
  deliberately by leaving.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE KEYING, which is the reason any of this matters:
media keys come from the child group's epoch (draft-atwood-mimi-calls
§4.3), so a departed user keeps media access until the removal commits.
That is the same window operator removal already has. The draft's claim
that "a participant removed from the call loses access to subsequent
media at once" holds for a removal FROM THE CALL, which is a Commit; it
does not hold for a cascade from the parent, and §4.4 of the draft should
say so rather than leave the reader to work it out.

NOTE FOR THE DRAFT: that last paragraph is a correction to
draft-atwood-mimi-calls, not just a mimid note. Filed as a follow-up.
